question: In loops of five to eight rule-60 rings with law (12, 12), does every balanced loop (positions summing to rs/2) keep every contact binding both its rings, and which unbalanced loops do too?

public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 16 worker processes.
public_inputs.family: r = 5 to 8 rings of s = 4 to 16 cells, contact positions from {2, floor(s/2), ceil(s/2), s - 2}, one loop per rotation class: 65,472 loops.
public_inputs.exactness: Rows of M^T exactly to lag 400: a contact misses a ring at the first lag its row meets none of the ring's cells. Persistence beyond lag 400 is not decided here; for balanced loops it is LOOP-ANY-20261108-001A's theorem.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the family after seeing results
primary_observable: Balanced loops that miss a ring or whose witnesses fail (H1 predicts none); unbalanced loops that persist to lag 400.
cheapest_meaningful_control: net_lib agrees with path_lib and with its full-state-space reading (SEPARATE-20261108-001A, check 1); the four-ring case is LOOP-PROOF-20261108-001A, checked to size 30.
decision_or_followup_rule: H1, frozen: every balanced loop keeps its chain-end witnesses to lag 400. If it holds, it supports the theorem at r = 5 to 8; if any balanced loop fails, the theorem's proof is wrong and is withdrawn.
stop_rule: Stop when every loop of the family has its verdict to lag 400.
nonclaims: Exploratory: lags to 400, these positions only.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing: a probe of random positions in loops of 3 and 5 to 8 rings at sizes 4 to 12 found all 1,294 balanced loops persisting to lag 300 and some unbalanced ones persisting too. run.py --pilot timed 300 random loops at 1.3 s and printed no verdicts.
